expectations.text: Three title options, each using a visibly different strategy
expectations.evidence: Three titles delivered: 'How a Dockerfile Reorder...' (how/trigger), 'Why Our Builds Took 40 Minutes Until a New Hire Asked One Question' (story/why), 'A 12-Minute Build Became a 40-Minute Build. We Had No Metric for Why.' (number-driven). Each labeled with its strategy.

expectations.text: One title marked as recommended with a stated reason
expectations.evidence: Title 1 marked '*recommended*. Clear, specific, and honest; it names the cause and the surprising outcome without clickbait.'

expectations.text: Titles use trigger word OR number (not both crammed), avoid 'things'
expectations.evidence: No 'things'. Title 2 mixes 'Why' with '40 Minutes' (borderline vs the 'rarely both' guidance), but titles 1 and 3 follow the rule cleanly.

expectations.text: Titles avoid clickbait adjectives while making a concrete promise
expectations.evidence: No unbelievable/incredible/mind-blowing; promises (cause of 3x CI slowdown) delivered by the post.

expectations.text: Writing plan includes a working title drafted before writing
expectations.evidence: Phase 3 plan opens with 'Working title: How a Dockerfile Reorder Quietly Tripled Our CI Time'.

expectations.text: Section subheadings carry a concrete point/promise, not generic labels
expectations.evidence: 'The question we should have asked months earlier', 'The fix was small; the guardrail mattered more' — all concrete, no 'Background'/'The Problem'.

expectations.text: Story-first opening, ~1000-1400 words, no banned phrases
expectations.evidence: Opens with new hire's question; agent-verified 1,399 words; banned-phrase scan clean.

expectations.text: All facts trace to notes; gaps marked [FILL: ...]
expectations.evidence: 40/12 min, 3x, 6 months, COPY reorder, cache metric all from notes; stack-specific commands left as [FILL: ...] rather than invented.
